opened.title: Pull request (PR)
opened.definition: A proposal to add changes to the main code. A person has to review and accept it before it lands.

quiz.text: ✓ Right. On a greenfield idea the cheapest question is "is this the right problem at all?" — asked before any product shape or technical detail exists. That is the office-hours step.

choice.output: All screens firstHorizontal — five booking screens that don't save anything. Pick one workflow (book a slot) and make it work end-to-end instead.

drive390.shipText: Agent · pre-PR 01On a branch?02Recover if not03Tests & build04Fresh verify05Update docs06Commit07Push branch08Exact PR handback PR link ↓ Human · GitHub 01Open the PR02Read summary03Skim files04Check CI05Mark ready06Merge the PR "merged" ↓ Agent · post-merge 01Confirm merge02Verify state03Post-merge?04Next action05latest pulled · fresh branch started
drive390.responsibilityText: Human You Make the important decisions explicit. Describe what to build, in plain language. Answer product questions when the agent asks. Review and normally merge the PR; decide whether the project may use K4.1. Tell the agent when to ship and what to do next. Agent The agent Do the work; show the work; never self-approve. Read the project's ground rules and the words your project uses. Clarify before coding when the request is non-trivial. Branch, build vertical slices, test as you go. Run fresh independent verification before the exact PR handback.

accessibleNames.name: Human owns intent and approval; agent owns execution and verification. Intent flows from human to agent; a pull request flows from agent back to human for review.
A five-stage development loop. Align, Slice, Build, Review and correct, Ship. After Ship a curved arrow returns to Align for the next feature.

The default manual-merge route. The agent confirms the branch, runs checks, uses a fresh verifier, updates documents, commits, pushes, and hands back the exact pull request. The human reviews and merges it. Control returns to the agent, which confirms the merge, verifies state, checks post-merge steps, and recommends what comes next.
